p: the heathen are come into thine: The people cry to God against the barbarous tyranny of the Babylonians who spoiled God's inheritance, polluted his temple, destroyed his religion, and murdered his people.
dead bodies of thy servants have: The prophets show to what extremities God sometimes allows his Church to fall to exercise their faith, before he sets his hand to deliver them.
bury them: Their friends and relatives did not dare to bury them for fear of the enemies.
neighbours: Of which some came from Abraham but were degenerate: and others were open enemies to your religion, but they both laughed at our miseries.
burn like fire: Will you completely consume us for our sins, before you take us to mercy?
former iniquities: Which we and our fathers have committed.
salvation: Seeing we have no other Saviour, neither can we help ourselves, and also by our salvation your Name will be praised: therefore O Lord, help us.
prisoner come before thee: Who though in respect to God they were justly punished for their sins, yet in consideration of their cause were unjustly murdered.
those that are appointed to die: Who were captives among their enemies and could look for nothing but death.
we will shew forth thy praise: We ought to desire no benefit from God, but on this condition to praise his name, Isa 43:21.
